question: A charity plans to have Claude pre-screen grant applications and produce a shortlist that trustees then review. Which two safeguards matter most before the charity starts? Select two.
options: A) Applications are gathered into a single file so that the whole set fits inside one continuous conversation.
B) The criteria Claude applies are written down and match the criteria the charity published to applicants.
C) Trustees read the applications Claude ranked lowest before any of them are set aside without funding.
D) The charity times each shortlisting round so it can report how many staff hours the new approach has saved.
E) The shortlist is produced on the most capable model available, so the ranking is more accurate.
correct_answers: B) The criteria Claude applies are written down and match the criteria the charity published to applicants.
C) Trustees read the applications Claude ranked lowest before any of them are set aside without funding.
explanations: How the files are packaged is a convenience question and has no bearing on whether the screening is fair or reviewable.
Correct. Applicants were judged against published criteria, so the screening must apply those same criteria and they must be inspectable.
Correct. For a different reason: it keeps the harmful outcome recoverable, because a wrongly down-ranked application can still be rescued by a person.
Measuring time saved is useful for the business case but does nothing to protect applicants from an unfair screen.
A stronger model does not make a rights-affecting screen safe, and model choice is not the governance safeguard here.
